text: power distribution (transformers and panel boards) for small power consumers Page63 of158 T-RICH Pre-FEED Report – Public Version The small power distribution system will supply lighting, small power receptacles, system control panels, UPS and other utilities and process related small power consumers. 4.4.4 UPS POWER DISTRIBUTION Battery backed UPS will supply power to consumers that require an uninterruptible power supply. The preliminary UPS design comprises two redundant UPS (A and B) located in the electrical room of the main site building. The preliminary UPS and battery rack information currently included in the MEL is based on a per-unit rating of 50 kVA; however, this will be evaluated further in the next study phase as the design matures and UPS load demand is better defined. The specific battery technology will also be evaluated further in the next study phase to determine whether more traditional valve-regulated lead acid batteries or lithium-ion batteries are preferred. Each UPS will supply a main distribution panel board, which will in turn supply the various electrical consumers that require UPS power. The typical consumers connected to the UPS system are process control cabinets, telecoms control cabinets, public address, general alarm equipment, fire detection system cabinets, aviation obstruction lights, and variable frequency drive control power. A detailed UPS load list will be developed in a future study phase, which will be used for final dimensioning of the UPS and battery banks based on the selected battery technology, calculated operating load, required runtime and applicable regulations. 4.4.5 ELECTRICALLY DRIVEN MOTOR LOADS Most of the electrical consumers for the facility will be motor driven. This includes the main process equipment (e.g., CO compressors) and associated auxiliary equipment and the various utilities systems. 2 Several of those consumers require speed control, which will be achieved using variable frequency motor drives. The remainder of the motor driven loads will be supplied direct-on-line (i.e., full voltage) by the supplying switchgear. The rating, location, and supply voltage of each VFD will be determined by the rating of the motor load that it is supplying. The preliminary design is based on VFDs for loads less than 30 kW located integrally within the supplying switchgear / motor control center, while VFDs for larger loads will be standalone (freestanding) units located in the electrical room. The largest VFDs are for the CO Compressors and will 2 be powered from the main 13.8 kV switchgear via dedicated VFD input transformers, which are in the outdoor substation. The VFD input transformers are intended to be liquid filled with an environmentally friendly, natural, or synthetic based ester. The specific variable frequency drive technology for the CO Compressor motors will be further evaluated 2 in the next study phase. The current design is based on a voltage source inverter (VSI) controller, while a load commutated inverter (LCI) controller is also a technically feasible option.
